s0501.literal: Many years passed: "many" was originally corrupted to "each"; the Southern Supervisory edition misread "name"; now corrected according to the Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall editions.
s0501.idiomatic: On "through many years": the text originally read each for many and the Southern Supervisory read name; corrected per the Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall editions.

s0504.literal: [Cong]—corrected according to the Annals of Emperor Wu in the History of the Southern Dynasties.
s0504.idiomatic: [Cong]—corrected per the Southern Dynasties Annals of Emperor Wu.

s0505.literal: Comment: the Biography of King Bi of Wu in the Records of the Grand Historian reads "had someone cong-kill the King of Wu"—this phrase derives from it.
s0505.idiomatic: The Records' Biography of King Bi of Wu reads "had someone cong-kill the King of Wu"—this line comes from there.

s0506.literal: Comment: cong means strike; cheng also means strike, but the text should follow the Records and read cong.
s0506.idiomatic: Note: cong means to strike and cheng likewise, but the Records' reading cong should be followed.

s0507.literal: Gold beast tally, first through fifth, left: "gold beast tally" is "gold tiger tally"—changed to avoid Tang taboo.
s0507.idiomatic: On "gold beast tally, first through fifth, left": gold beast tally is gold tiger tally, emended for Tang taboo.

s0508.literal: Bamboo envoy tally, first through tenth [left]—[left] supplied according to the Annals of Emperor Wu in the History of the Southern Dynasties.
s0508.idiomatic: On "bamboo envoy tally, first through tenth [left]": left restored per the Southern Dynasties Annals of Emperor Wu.

s0509.literal: Comment: under the tally system, tiger tallies and bamboo envoy tallies were each split into left and right.
s0509.idiomatic: Under the tally system, tiger tallies and bamboo envoy tallies were each divided into left and right halves.

s0510.literal: Therefore grant to the Duke three hundred warriors of the martial guard: "martial guard" is "tiger guard"—changed to avoid Tang taboo.
s0510.idiomatic: On "grant the Duke three hundred warriors of the martial guard": martial guard is tiger guard, changed for Tang taboo.

s0511.literal: Faintly the imperial apex: the Jigu edition has a small note below "faintly faintly" reading "also written huihui."
s0511.idiomatic: On "faintly the imperial apex": the Jigu edition notes below faintly faintly an alternate reading huihui.

s0512.literal: The Northern Supervisory, Hall editions, and the Annals of Emperor Wu in the History of the Southern Dynasties all read huihui.
s0512.idiomatic: The Northern Supervisory, Hall editions, and the Southern Dynasties Annals of Emperor Wu all read huihui.

s0515.idiomatic: argues that reading faintly faintly is correct.

s0516.literal: Dragon gait, martial stride: "martial stride" is "tiger stride"—changed to avoid Tang taboo.
s0516.idiomatic: On "dragon gait, martial stride": martial stride is tiger stride, changed for Tang taboo.

s0517.literal: The vicious chieftain's head sent: "chieftain" was originally corrupted to "gather"; other editions are not corrupt; now corrected.
s0517.idiomatic: On "the vicious chieftain's head sent": qu was originally miswritten as ji; other editions are correct; emended.

s0518.literal: The clepsydra drips into the deep spring: "deep spring" is "abyss spring"—changed to avoid Tang taboo.
s0518.idiomatic: On "the clepsydra drips into the deep spring": deep spring is abyss spring, changed for Tang taboo.

s0521.literal: [Yu]—corrected according to the Southern Supervisory edition.

s0522.literal: Comment: the Hall edition also follows the Southern Supervisory in the change.
s0522.idiomatic: The Hall edition likewise follows the Southern Supervisory emendation.

s0523.literal: Now dispatching the envoy bearing staff of office, concurrent Grand Tutor, Palace Attendant, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Marquis of Pingle precinct, Wang Tong—comment:
s0523.idiomatic: On "Now dispatching the envoy bearing staff, concurrent Grand Tutor, Palace Attendant, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Marquis of Pingle precinct, Wang Tong"—note:

s0525.literal: reads: "Tong served Liang as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and only on entering Chen was transferred to Left Vice Director."
s0525.idiomatic: reads: Tong served Liang as right vice director of the Masters of Writing and was not moved to left vice director until he entered Chen.

s0526.literal: Moreover Tong, as the emperor's sister's son, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuyang precinct.
s0526.idiomatic: Moreover, as the emperor's sister's son, he was enfeoffed Marquis of Wuyang precinct.

s0527.idiomatic: The annals and the biography disagree.
